entry.title: Former Hubei CSRC Bureau Party Secretary and Director Wang Guangyou Expelled from the Party
entry.summary: 湖北证监局原党委书记、局长王广幼被开除党籍 中国证监会 · Sep 28, 2026 The disciplinary and supervisory team of the CCDI and National Supervisory Commission stationed at the China Securities Regulatory Commission, together with the Hubei Supervisory Commission, investigated serious violations of discipline and law by Wang Guangyou, former party secretary and director of the Hubei CSRC bureau. The investigation found he accepted gifts and cash, borrowed money from regulated entities, traded stocks, and sought benefits in regulatory and enforcement matters. The CSRC party committee decided to expel him from the Party, illegal gains were confiscated, and the suspected criminal matter was transferred to prosecutors for review.

entry.title: CSRC seeks public comment on draft rules for public fund operations
entry.summary: 中国证监会就《公开募集证券投资基金运作管理办法（征求意见稿）》及配套规则公开征求意见 中国证监会 · Oct 9, 2026 The China Securities Regulatory Commission has opened public comment on a revised Measures for the Administration of Public Offering of Securities Investment Fund Operations and two supporting rules. The revisions aim to implement a plan promoting high-quality development of public funds, including tighter investment operation oversight, support for equity funds, and adjusted supervisory indicators. Feedback will inform the final rules before issuance.

entry.title: CSRC Holds Expert Symposium on Capital Markets and Financial Conditions With Listed Companies and Securities Firms
entry.summary: 中国证监会召开资本市场和金融形势专家座谈会 中国证监会 · Oct 10, 2026 On October 10, 2026, CSRC Party Secretary and Chairman Wu Qing chaired a symposium in Beijing with listed company executives and securities and fund industry experts on capital markets and financial conditions. Participants said the economy is stable and improving and capital markets are operating steadily. They proposed strengthening market stabilization mechanisms, widening medium- and long-term capital inflows, encouraging dividends and buybacks, optimizing IPO rules, and strengthening trading supervision.

entry.title: CSRC Chairman Wu Qing Meets with Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak of Mubadala Investment Company
entry.summary: 吴清主席会见阿联酋穆巴达拉投资公司首席执行官兼董事总经理哈勒敦 中国证监会 · Oct 12, 2026 On October 12, 2026, CSRC Chairman Wu Qing met in Beijing with Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak, CEO and Managing Director of Mubadala Investment Company, a sovereign investment institution of the UAE. The two sides exchanged views on the international economic and financial situation, strengthening capital market cooperation between China and the UAE, and expanding investment in China.

entry.title: CSRC Issues Rules on Administrative Penalties for Illegal Securities Transfers, Effective December 1, 2026
entry.summary: 中国证监会发布《违规转让证券案件行政处罚实施规则》 中国证监会 · Oct 19, 2026 The China Securities Regulatory Commission issued the Implementing Rules on Administrative Penalties for Cases of Illegal Securities Transfer on October 19, 2026, effective December 1, 2026. The eighteen-article rules define illegal securities transfers and divide them into four categories. Each category has its own discretionary penalty benchmarks, and the rules also cover penalty adjustment factors, combined penalties, special cases, and market bans.

entry.title: CSRC official answers questions on rules for penalizing illegal securities transfers
entry.summary: 中国证监会有关部门负责人就《违规转让证券案件行政处罚实施规则》答记者问 中国证监会 · Oct 19, 2026 On October 19, 2026, the China Securities Regulatory Commission issued the Implementing Rules on Administrative Penalties for Illegal Securities Transfer Cases, comprising 18 articles. The rules divide illegal securities transfers into four categories and set mitigating, general, and aggravating penalty tiers based on the violation ratio and amount. They also specify penalty circumstances and the handling of cases involving both illegal transfers and information disclosure violations.

entry.title: CSRC Seeks Public Comment on Securities Market Advance Compensation Guidelines
entry.summary: 中国证监会就《证券市场先行赔付指导意见》公开征求意见 中国证监会 · Oct 19, 2026 The China Securities Regulatory Commission has drafted guidelines to standardize advance compensation under Article 93 of the Securities Law, aiming to make it more transparent and predictable for resolving mass securities disputes. The draft sets out who may apply advance compensation, its basic positioning and main procedures, the entrustment services and scope of investor protection bodies, and coordination among relevant parties. It also states support for advance compensation, which may be considered in administrative licensing, penalty discretion and integrity supervision. Public comments are invited.

entry.title: CSRC seeks public comment on draft rules for private investment master funds
entry.summary: 中国证监会就《私募投资母基金管理规定（征求意见稿）》公开征求意见 中国证监会 · Oct 23, 2026 The China Securities Regulatory Commission has drafted the Administrative Provisions on Private Investment Master Funds and opened them for public comment. The draft has 23 articles covering definitions and classification, diversified investment requirements, exemption from the first investment tier, ongoing requirements for managers, operational management, and an investment negative list.[sic]

entry.title: CSRC Chairman Wu Qing Meets Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan's Delegation
entry.summary: 吴清主席会见香港特区政府财政司司长陈茂波一行 中国证监会 · Oct 23, 2026 On October 23, 2026, CSRC Chairman Wu Qing met Hong Kong SAR Financial Secretary Paul Chan and SFC Chief Executive Julia Leung. They exchanged views on supporting Hong Kong's implementation of the first Five-Year Plan, deepening practical cooperation between the two markets, and strengthening Hong Kong's position as an international financial center.[X]

entry.title: Keynote speech by CSRC Chairman Wu Qing at the 2026 Financial Street Forum, outlining capital market development plans for China's 15th Five-Year Plan period.
entry.summary: 统筹发展和安全 坚持开放与合作 奋力谱写资本市场“十五五”高质量发展新篇章——吴清主席在2026金融街论坛年会上的主题演讲 中国证监会 · Oct 19, 2026 The speech reviews listed companies' first-half earnings, dividends and buybacks, and analyzes risks from geopolitical conflict, interest-rate shifts, artificial intelligence and cross-market linkages. It sets out four priorities: maintaining market stability, inclusive institutional reform, strict enforcement under the law, and wider opening to foreign investors. It also outlines development plans for Beijing's capital market and the Beijing Stock Exchange.
